record.paper_title: Recent Results and Open Problems in Evolutionary Multiobjective Optimization
record.original_question: How should parallel multi-objective evolutionary algorithms be architected for expensive optimization problems: should they maintain local external archives or one global archive, can independent demes search non-overlapping regions of the search space, and can GPU-based implementations be made efficient and effective?

evidence.quote: should we use local external archives or only a global one?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a multi-objective optimization problem of the form: minimize F(x) = (f_1(x), ..., f_m(x)) over a search space S, where each evaluation of F is computationally expensive. A multi-objective evolutionary algorithm (MOEA) maintains a population of candidate solutions and iteratively applies variation and selection operators to approximate the Pareto-optimal set { x in S : there is no y in S with f_i(y) <= f_i(x) for all i and strict inequality for some i }. An external archive is an auxiliary set storing non-dominated solutions encountered during the run.

A parallel MOEA partitions its computation across multiple processing units (e.g., demes in an island model, or GPU threads). Investigate the following architectural questions for parallel MOEAs applied to expensive multi-objective problems:

(a) Determine under what conditions maintaining a separate local external archive per deme (parallel subpopulation) yields a better final Pareto-set approximation, in terms of standard quality indicators such as hypervolume and inverted generational distance, than maintaining a single global external archive shared among all demes, and conversely.

(b) Design and analyze a scheme in which independent demes are constrained to search non-overlapping regions of the search space S (i.e., S is partitioned into disjoint subregions S_1, ..., S_k, each assigned to one deme), and determine whether such region partitioning can provably preserve coverage of the Pareto front while reducing redundant function evaluations compared with demes searching the full space.

(c) Provide GPU-based implementations of MOEAs together with a complexity and empirical efficiency analysis demonstrating both speedup (efficiency) and preservation of solution quality (effectiveness) relative to sequential and CPU-parallel baselines on benchmark expensive multi-objective problems.
artifact.status_search_result: The questions concern open architectural design problems in parallel multi-objective evolutionary algorithms, particularly for expensive optimization. Survey literature and recent work indicate that the trade-offs between local versus global archives, region-decomposition strategies for islands/demes, and efficient GPU-based MOEA implementations remain active research topics with no definitive resolution; partial results exist (e.g., specific GPU implementations of NSGA-II/MOEA-D and decomposition-based island models) but a general answer is not established.

status_evidence.title: A Survey on GPU-Based Implementation of Swarm Intelligence Algorithms
status_evidence.snippet: Surveys GPU implementations of population-based metaheuristics, noting open challenges in efficiency and effectiveness for multi-objective variants.
status_evidence.claim: GPU-based MOEA design remains an active research area with open questions.

status_evidence.title: Parallel Multi-Objective Evolutionary Algorithms: A Comprehensive Survey
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses archive management (local vs global) and island/deme architectures as open design questions for parallel MOEAs.
status_evidence.claim: Local vs global archive and deme partitioning are recognized open architectural questions.
